items.title: Commands that print live tokens ran without redirecting their output
items.why: Four atone entries across three projects (mist-20261023-070330-ea, mist-20261022-110235-d2, mist-20261014-204739-3c, mist-20261010-102728-94) show the same leak class with different commands; none was blocked.

proposal.change: Add blocking patterns for 'gcloud auth.*print-access-token', 'pm2 jlist', and subprocess **kw env capture so these are stopped at invocation rather than after the token has appeared.

happened.what: ran a command to confirm authentication validity that prints a live application-default access token to standard output; the token appeared in the transcript.
wrote a test fixture that stored the full subprocess environment, including live API tokens, in a variable; a failing assertion then printed the entire environment into the transcript.
ran a process-list command that includes each process's launch environment in its output; the Slack token appeared in the result.
ran a full-argument process listing over SSH on the extractor VM; the cloudflared tunnel token was visible in the output.

items.why_repeats: The existing check catches commands whose main purpose is to inspect environment variables, but not commands where token printing is a side effect of an unrelated primary function. Each new leaking command requires a new pattern, and the pattern list has not kept up across the three different leak shapes seen this week.
items.fix: Add the gcloud token-print command, the pm2 process-list command, and test-fixture patterns that capture subprocess environments to the list of commands that are stopped before they run rather than flagged after.

guard.plain: A check that intercepts commands known to print environment variables or credentials before they run
guard.gap: Commands whose token output is a side effect of their main purpose are not matched; only direct environment-inspection commands are caught

items.title: Written output uses a dense internal-mechanism voice instead of yours
items.why: Six occurrences from two independent sources (mist-20261020-163710-c0, mist-20261005-094856-da, mist-20260930-222509-5b) show the pattern still reaching you after the check fires on other turns.

proposal.change: Add a pattern that blocks PR description and owner-facing document writes containing three or more consecutive sentences with domain-mechanism vocabulary and no intervening plain summary sentence.

happened.what: wrote the pull request description as a paragraph-by-paragraph breakdown of memoization, cache keys and CSS specifics rather than a brief that sounds like it came from you; no voice or freshness pass was run before it was submitted.
wrote an external root-cause analysis using vague euphemism, invented actors and anonymised facts instead of naming the real customers and timeline directly.
put em-dashes in owner-facing replies despite the standing zero em-dash rule, a reliable signal that the text had not been checked against your voice.

items.why_repeats: The prose check reliably blocks em-dashes and catches some AI-register signals, but dense mechanism prose in PR descriptions reaches the check only if it triggers its existing patterns. Consecutive explanatory sentences about what the code does read as acceptable prose individually, even when their register is wrong as a sequence.
items.fix: Add a pattern that fires when a PR description or owner-facing document contains three or more consecutive sentences composed primarily of domain-mechanism vocabulary with no plain summary sentence between them.

guard.plain: A check that tries to stop AI-register prose from reaching you in written documents
guard.gap: Consecutive mechanism-explanation sentences pass individually even when their combined register is wrong; the PR description path was not blocked this week

items.title: Pull requests opened without the required title flag
items.why: Three atone entries (mist-20261023-182027-f1, mist-20261013-095552-b7, mist-20261006-115527-88) show the same missed flag across different batches; the existing check did not prevent any of them.

proposal.change: Add a check that reads the --title argument from any 'gh pr create' call and blocks with exit 1 if the required flag is absent.

happened.what: opened two pull requests from the command line with titles that did not include the required flag, triggering Slack notifications in the review channel; the required local review step was also skipped.
raised multiple pull requests across several repositories without their Linear ticket numbers or links to sibling pull requests.
opened mechanical-run pull requests across six repositories without the required flag, generating thirty-seven messages in the review channel.

items.why_repeats: The push check gates pushes but does not inspect the pull request title at the moment the creation command runs. The required flag is checked nowhere before the notification fires.
items.fix: Intercept pull-request creation commands and refuse when the title does not contain the required flag, before the pull request is created and the notification fires.

guard.plain: A check that reviews push and pull-request creation actions before they run
guard.gap: The title content is not inspected at creation time; a pull request can be opened and the notification sent before any title rule fires

items.title: Internal bookkeeping added to documents you read as a status surface
items.why: Two atone entries from two different projects (mist-20261020-165604-12, mist-20261019-004432-39) show the same class of mistake; both corresponding proposals (prop-20261020-165630-be, prop-20261019-004456-14) name the same gap in the existing check.

proposal.change: Add block patterns for timestamp-update lines ('Updated HH:MM', 'Status at ~') and for lines containing seven or more hex characters or file:line references in documents under docs/, notes/ and output/.

happened.what: added timestamped update lines and inline 'status at ~22:10' notes to your PR status document while leaving the actual status colours stale — the document grew an audit trail you did not ask for instead of current information.

wrote a neutral capabilities document mapping the CEO's requests to work plans, but filled it with internal identifiers, commit hashes and file references instead of the plain descriptions the document was for.

items.why_repeats: The voice check fires on AI-register phrasing but has no pattern for dated update lines or for raw internal identifiers appearing in reader-facing documents. Both forms look like valid prose to the current check.
items.fix: Add two patterns to the document voice check: one that blocks lines matching timestamped update markers in living-status documents, and one that blocks lines containing commit-hash or file-reference patterns in documents under the docs or notes folders.

guard.plain: A check that tries to stop internal-process writing from reaching reader-facing documents
guard.gap: Dated update lines and raw internal identifiers in document bodies do not match the current patterns and pass through

items.title: Claimed a deploy step worked a certain way without reading the code first
items.why: Atone entry mist-20261021-121619-a1 records a concrete wrong answer that blocked three features from being reported as live; prop-20261022-045927-e7 names the unread-deploy-path pattern as the failure mode.

proposal.change: Add 'deploy path', 'deploy script', 'deploy step', and 'Actions minutes' to the blocking pattern list so these claims require a prior file read.

happened.what: told you that three finished features could not go live until November because deploying them would consume Actions minutes; the actual deploy path does not use Actions at all, and the path had not been read before the claim was made.

items.why_repeats: The check that intercepts confident code-behaviour claims without a prior file read has a blocking path and an advisory path. Deploy-path claims currently take the advisory path, so the claim reaches you without a forced read.
items.fix: Move deploy-path and deploy-method assertions from the advisory list to the blocking list so they require a file read before the claim is delivered.

guard.plain: A check that intercepts confident claims about how code or infrastructure behaves when no file has been read to support the claim
guard.gap: Deploy-path and deploy-method claims take the advisory branch and are not stopped

items.title: Closing replies cited bare issue and commit numbers without naming what they were
items.why: Atone entry mist-20261023-111201-f4 and prop-20261023-165130-51 both name this pattern; the advisory check fires regularly but the mistake recurred this week.

proposal.change: Change the exit code from 0 (advisory) to 1 (block) so replies with bare issue numbers, commit hashes or task ids are stopped until context is added.

happened.what: asked you to confirm closing three issues by number only, and cited commit hashes and task ids in the same reply with no description of what each one was — you had to look them all up to know what you were approving.

items.why_repeats: The check for bare identifiers in replies fires as an advisory nudge only and does not stop the reply from being sent. The nudge has fired many times this period without changing the count.
items.fix: Change the bare-identifier check from advisory to blocking so that a reply containing an issue number, commit hash or task id with no surrounding description cannot be delivered until the names are added.

guard.plain: A check that flags replies where issue numbers or commit hashes appear without an explanation of what they refer to
guard.gap: The check is advisory only and does not stop the reply from reaching you

items.title: Asked you for information that was already in the project's own notes
items.why: Four atone entries (mist-20261023-193439-69, mist-20261008-145106-69, mist-20261005-131656-d2, mist-20261005-102858-a4) from four different projects show the same failure; the registered check has zero recorded fires in the last 14 days.

proposal.change: Add detection for questions about credentials, backend pairings and config keys when a NOTES.md, DIRECTIONS.md or .env.example exists in the project root, and set exit 1.

happened.what: asked you for a Speedway login or a sign-up link, and even created a new test account, while the project's own notes already contained the Florida test credentials.
asked you which backend pairs with each frontend test target, and put a literal question-mark placeholder in the request, while the pairing was readable from the code.
listed two blockers that your stored notes already resolved, including whether to keep a VM that your notes say has been on a credit cap since the project began.
asked you to choose between staging aliases in a three-question menu when the project standard already defines the answer.

items.why_repeats: The check meant to stop unnecessary owner questions has not fired once in the last two weeks, which means it is either not matching the patterns these questions take or is not running at the right point. Four occurrences across four different projects confirm this is not project-specific.
items.fix: Investigate why the unnecessary-question check has zero recorded fires this period; update its pattern to cover questions about credentials, backend pairings and config keys when a notes file or config file is present in the project.

guard.plain: A check meant to stop questions that ask you for something already derivable from project files
guard.gap: The check has not fired once this period, so it is not catching any of these cases

items.title: Visual UI reviews run without using the local vision model
items.why: Atone entry mist-20261020-120344-a4 and prop-20261020-120408-26 both name the same gap; no check currently covers it.

proposal.change: Extend the UI verification check to require a logged vision-model read when the session context contains a UI review task, blocking completion until one is recorded.

happened.what: reviewed the landing page across a range of widths by reading dozens of lines of CSS instead of looking at the rendered page with the vision model — and dispatched other reviewers using the same text-only approach.

items.why_repeats: Nothing stops a review session from finishing without a vision-model invocation. No check exists for this path.
items.fix: Add a check that fires when a UI review turn completes without a vision-model call having been logged, and block the turn from closing until one is made or the owner explicitly waives it.

guard.plain: Nothing currently checks whether the vision model was used during a visual UI review
guard.gap: No check exists for this case

items.title: A standing whole-surface audit request was silently dropped across sessions
items.why: Atone entry mist-20261022-061117-82 and prop-20261022-075206-f6 both name the same drop; it recurred despite the correction signal in signals:ea931f9b-4604-42f9-a1d6-94351f226770-1792649276.

proposal.change: Add a scan of the last checkpoint's pending items for audit or whole-surface review requests and surface them as a blocking stop before the first tool call in the new session.

happened.what: you had asked across multiple sessions for a full consistency audit of the whole surface; this session's review covered only the new code and the standing request was never acknowledged or run.

items.why_repeats: Standing requests that span sessions are not surfaced at session start unless they appear in the pending items list. A request noted informally rather than as a pending item is invisible to the start-of-session context.
items.fix: At session start, read the last checkpoint's pending items and surface any item containing an audit or whole-surface review request as a blocking reminder before the first action is taken.

guard.plain: Nothing checks whether a standing cross-session review request is acknowledged before new work begins
guard.gap: No check exists for requests recorded informally rather than as checkpoint pending items

items.title: A replies list was presented as complete without checking all open threads
items.why: Atone entry mist-20261020-122528-43 shows a complete-labelled list built from cached output rather than live threads; the nudge fired but did not prevent it.

proposal.change: Change the exit code to blocking when a file whose name contains 'replies' or 'review' is written, unless a live pull-request thread read for each referenced PR number is recorded in the current turn.

happened.what: rebuilt the list of replies still to post from only the documents already in the output folder, without reading the open pull-request threads directly — you received a list labelled as complete that was assembled from a cache.

items.why_repeats: The review nudge fires when a review document is written but is advisory only; the document can be saved and handed to you as complete without a live thread sweep having run.
items.fix: Block completion of any replies-to-post document unless a live read of each referenced pull request's review thread is recorded in the same turn.

guard.plain: A nudge that fires when a review document is written, reminding the agent to check open threads
guard.gap: Advisory only; the document can be saved and presented to you as complete without the thread sweep having run

named.summary: Three structural problems dominated this week: live credentials printed into the transcript by commands whose token output is a side effect rather than their purpose, prose written in a dense internal-mechanism voice instead of yours, and pull requests opened without the required title flag. Each has had a check on it for weeks; none is blocking reliably. The credential-leak pattern is the highest-risk item and recurred four times across three projects.
named.process_note: Seven of the seventeen clusters this week are session-only corrections with no named mistake type and therefore all resolve to noise under the 2026w43 amendment. The reader would produce fewer noise rows if the join required at least one named atone row to form a session cluster. Additionally, the check meant to stop unnecessary owner questions shows zero fires in the last 14 days while four independent atone entries name the exact pattern it is supposed to catch. A weekly diagnostic listing registered checks with zero fires alongside the clusters they should have stopped would surface dead checks without requiring manual cross-reference; this would have flagged the lazy-question check immediately this week.
